title: Jacob's Years in Haran
rules: Use original Story Adventure wheel, free contextual hint + 15 and 25-token thinking hints, no letter purchase on Episode 11; only JW.org links, no new game mode

discoveries.title: The Stone at the Well
discoveries.narration: Jacob reaches the land of the people of the East and sees shepherds beside a well. A large stone covers its opening. Then Rachel arrives with her father's sheep! Jacob moves the stone and waters her flock. What a way to meet a relative.

interaction.prompt: What did Jacob roll away before watering Rachel's sheep?

progressiveHints.text: The flocks had gathered, but they still couldn't drink.
Something heavy covered the water.
Jacob moved it away from the mouth of the well.

discoveries.explanation: Jacob rolled the large stone away from the mouth of the well and watered the sheep belonging to Laban. The Bible doesn't tell us that the shepherds couldn't have moved it—only that Jacob did. (Genesis 29:1–10)

discoveries.title: A Welcome in Haran
discoveries.narration: Rachel runs to tell Laban that Rebekah's son has arrived. Laban hurries to meet Jacob, embraces him, and brings him home. Jacob has traveled far, but here he finds relatives who recognize him.

interaction.prompt: After his long trip, Jacob found his mother's relatives. What kind of bond connected them?

progressiveHints.text: Laban already knew Jacob's mother.
Their connection wasn't a business arrangement.
Rebekah and Laban belonged to the same household of relatives.

discoveries.explanation: Laban was Rebekah's brother, and Jacob was Rebekah's son. Laban welcomed Jacob into his house after hearing who he was. (Genesis 29:12–14)

discoveries.title: Seven Years That Felt Short
discoveries.narration: Jacob loves Rachel. Laban asks him to name his wages, so Jacob offers to work seven years to marry her. The Bible says those years seemed like just a few days to him because he loved her. Seven years! That's a remarkable way to describe a long wait.

interaction.prompt: What made seven years of work feel like only a few days to Jacob?

progressiveHints.text: Think about how Jacob felt toward Rachel.
Long work can feel different when the reason matters deeply.
Genesis 29:20 gives his affection as the reason.

discoveries.explanation: Jacob worked seven years for Rachel, but the time seemed short because he loved her. That's the reason Genesis 29:20 itself gives. (Genesis 29:18–20)

discoveries.title: The Morning Surprise
discoveries.narration: The seven years end, and Laban holds a feast. But during the evening, he brings Leah instead of Rachel. When morning comes, Jacob discovers what happened and confronts Laban. The Bible doesn't soften that deception.

interaction.prompt: Whom did Laban bring to Jacob instead of Rachel?

progressiveHints.text: It was Laban's older daughter.
The two sisters were not treated fairly by Laban's decision.
Her name is given in Genesis 29:23–25.

discoveries.explanation: During the evening, Laban brought Leah to Jacob. Jacob discovered the deception in the morning and asked Laban why he had tricked him. (Genesis 29:21–26)

discoveries.title: A Difficult Agreement
discoveries.narration: Laban tells Jacob he can also marry Rachel after Leah's wedding week—but Jacob must work seven more years. Jacob agrees. The account doesn't invite us to pretend the family situation was simple; it tells us what happened.

interaction.prompt: What did Jacob agree to give Laban for another seven years?

progressiveHints.text: Jacob's payment wasn't a bag of coins.
He was expected to keep working for Laban.
Genesis 29:30 describes another seven years of work.

discoveries.explanation: Laban required Jacob to serve seven more years after he was given Rachel as a wife. (Genesis 29:27–30)

discoveries.title: Leah Gives Thanks
discoveries.narration: Leah feels the pain of being less loved. She becomes the mother of Reuben, Simeon, Levi, and Judah. When Judah is born, she says something beautiful: this time, she will praise Jehovah.

interaction.prompt: When Judah was born, what did Leah say she would give Jehovah?

progressiveHints.text: Leah wasn't talking about getting more possessions.
She wanted to honor Jehovah with her words.
Genesis 29:35 records an expression of gratitude to God.

discoveries.explanation: At the birth of Judah, Leah said that she would praise Jehovah. The Bible records her hurt as well as this expression of thanks. (Genesis 29:31–35)

discoveries.title: Rachel Welcomes Joseph
discoveries.narration: Rachel has waited so long for a child. The account says God remembers her and hears her. At last she has a son, and she calls him Joseph. Imagine the relief and happiness she must have felt!

interaction.prompt: What did Rachel name the son born after God heard her?

progressiveHints.text: She had long hoped to become a mother.
The name she chose also appears later in Genesis as a major Bible character.
Genesis 30:24 gives the child's name.

discoveries.explanation: God enabled Rachel to become pregnant and she gave birth to Joseph. She said Jehovah was adding another son to her. (Genesis 30:22–24)

discoveries.title: A Flock of His Own
discoveries.narration: Jacob wants to provide for his own household after years of work for Laban. They make an agreement about which animals will count as Jacob's wages. The spotted, patched, and dark-colored animals matter a lot in this chapter.

interaction.prompt: Which kind of marked animals were included in Jacob's agreed wages?

progressiveHints.text: Not all the animals in the agreement had one plain coat.
Think of small spots and patches among the sheep and goats.
Genesis 30:32 mentions animals with scattered spots.

discoveries.explanation: Jacob and Laban agreed that speckled, color-patched, and some dark-colored animals would be counted as Jacob's wages. The flocks grew in the years that followed. (Genesis 30:31–43)

discoveries.title: Jehovah Says Go Home
discoveries.narration: Things aren't going well between Jacob and Laban. Jacob sees that Laban's attitude has changed. Then Jehovah tells Jacob to return to the land of his relatives and promises to stay with him. Jacob speaks with Rachel and Leah, and they support the decision.

interaction.prompt: What did Jehovah tell Jacob to do when it was time to leave Laban's household?

progressiveHints.text: Jehovah wasn't telling Jacob to remain where he was.
The journey would take him toward his family and homeland.
He was told to go back to the land of his fathers.

discoveries.explanation: Jehovah told Jacob to return to the land of his fathers and relatives, promising to be with him. Jacob then explained the situation to Rachel and Leah. (Genesis 31:1–18)

discoveries.title: A Peaceful Parting
discoveries.narration: Laban catches up with Jacob after the family leaves. Both men have plenty to say, and the discussion becomes tense. Finally, they make a formal agreement and set up stones as a witness. It's an important step toward parting without further conflict.

interaction.prompt: What formal agreement did Jacob and Laban make before parting?

progressiveHints.text: It marked the end of their argument with a serious commitment.
The heap of stones served as a witness to their promise.
Genesis 31:44 describes making a formal bond between the men.

discoveries.explanation: Jacob and Laban made a covenant. They set up a pillar and a heap of stones as a witness to the agreement, and Laban returned home. (Genesis 31:43–55)
